question.text: A body is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed of 40 m/s. Taking the upward direction as positive and assuming g = 10 m/s², draw the acceleration-time (a-t), velocity-time (v-t), and displacement-time (s-t) curves representing its entire motion until it returns to the launch level.
conditions: acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²
motion considered from launch until return to the ground

figure.description:
Three kinematic graphs from t = 0 s to t = 8 s:
1. a-t graph: A horizontal line at a = −10 m/s² spanning from t = 0 s to t = 8 s.
2. v-t graph: A straight line with a constant negative slope beginning at (0 s, +40 m/s), intersecting the time axis at (4 s, 0 m/s), and ending at (8 s, −40 m/s).
3. s-t graph: An inverted parabola starting at the origin (0 s, 0 m), reaching a peak at (4 s, 80 m), and returning to zero at (8 s, 0 m).

solution.approach: Use the equations of motion under constant gravity with upward positive to find the times, then plot each quantity against time.

steps.text: Find the time to reach the highest point, where velocity becomes zero.
Find the total time of flight back to the starting point.
Describe the a-t graph: acceleration stays constant throughout, since gravity does not change.
steps.equation: a = −10 m/s² for the whole interval t = 0 to t = 8 s

steps.text: Describe the v-t graph using v = u + at.
steps.equation: v starts at +40 m/s at t = 0, falls in a straight line, crosses zero at t = 4 s, reaches −40 m/s at t = 8 s

steps.text: Describe the s-t graph using s = ut + ½at², which is symmetric about the highest point.
steps.equation: s rises from 0 to a peak of 80 m at t = 4 s, then falls back to 0 m at t = 8 s

final_answer.value: a-t graph: constant −10 m/s² from t = 0 to t = 8 s. v-t graph: a straight line from +40 m/s at t = 0 to −40 m/s at t = 8 s, crossing zero at t = 4 s. s-t graph: a curve rising from 0 to a peak of 80 m at t = 4 s and returning to 0 m at t = 8 s.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the acceleration as zero at the highest point, since velocity is zero there, confuses velocity with acceleration; gravity acts throughout at −10 m/s².
Using T = u/g = 4 s as the total flight time instead of 2u/g = 8 s stops the graphs halfway, missing the fall back to the ground.
